note: Literature establishes a specific peripheral blood DNA methylation episignature and CxxC subsignature for KDM2B variants used in diagnostic classification.

evidence.text: Pathogenic heterozygous variants in KDM2B are associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder and a shared epigenetic signature detectable in peripheral blood, with both loss-of-function and CxxC-domain missense variants presenting specific subsignatures.

source.title: Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and its associated DNA methylation signature
source.quote: Both loss-of-function and CxxC-domain missense variants present with a specific subepisignature. Moreover, the KDM2B episignature was identified in the context of a dual molecular diagnosis in multiple individuals.

numbers.metric: individuals recruited with heterozygous KDM2B variants
KDM2B variants supported as pathogenic by evidence including shared episignature

evidence.text: DNA methylation episignatures across Mendelian neurodevelopmental disorders enable highly accurate and disease-specific diagnostic classifiers across overlapping genetic syndromes.

source.title: Novel diagnostic DNA methylation episignatures expand and refine the epigenetic landscapes of Mendelian disorders
source.quote: We demonstrate increasing resolution and specificity ranging from protein complex, gene, sub-gene, protein domain, and even single nucleotide-level Mendelian episignatures. We show the power of multiclass modeling to develop highly accurate and disease-specific diagnostic classifiers.
